title: Joint control under a dynamic coolant loop (thermal mass + setpoint ramp limits)
research_question: Does the joint controller's advantage over independent control, and its thermal safety, survive when the coolant loop has thermal mass and the plant cannot move its outlet temperature instantly?
hypothesis: H1: joint uses less energy per successful task than independent (paired 95% CI below 0) in all 3 scenarios under both dynamic plants. H2: under the slow plant (150 kg, 0.25 K/min) joint records chip-seconds above the 80 C target in at least one scenario, because it plans against a steady state the plant cannot reach quickly. H3: the fixed policy's energy changes by less than 0.5% between quasi-steady and dynamic plants (its setpoint never moves). H4: joint_robust records no more chip-seconds above target than joint in every scenario and plant.
null_hypothesis: The joint advantage disappears (CI includes 0) under a dynamic plant, and loop dynamics do not affect thermal safety.
independent_variables: plant model (quasi-steady, 40 kg + 1 K/min, 150 kg + 0.25 K/min)
baseline: quasi-steady plant (identical to E001) within each policy; independent within each plant
configuration: Loop mass and ramp values are class F placeholders (CDU tank + piping), not measurements.
evaluation_criteria: Paired relative differences with 95% t-CI; practical threshold 1%. H2/H4 judged on seed means of chip-seconds above target.
known_limitations: Single well-mixed tank; no pipe transport delay; ramp limit is symmetric; controllers still plan with a steady-state twin.
disclosure: Before registration, only unit tests ran on the dynamic plant (energy closure, ramp bound, steady state, pass-through); none compared policies.
data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
